tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description starts with imperative phrasing 'Use this skill when the user wants to understand or cut Amazon Bedrock spend, or check Bedrock capacity', focuses on user intent/goals (why bill is high, which model costs most, token-spend drift, etc.) rather than implementation mechanics, and is pushy in explicitly enumerating many trigger contexts including cases where users don't name the domain directly (e.g., 'even if they don't call it a cost review'). It is a long run-on paragraph, which pushes conciseness, but the density is justified by the breadth of distinct trigger scenarios and it remains a single coherent sentence/paragraph rather than verbose prose.
tests.evidence: "Use this skill when the user wants to understand or cut Amazon Bedrock spend, or check Bedrock capacity, even if they don't call it a cost review, for example why the bill is high or suspiciously low..."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The skill body is dense but nearly all content is domain-specific: exact API names, grouping rules, label conventions, and rules unique to Bedrock cost analysis. There is no explanation of generic concepts like 'what is cost' or 'what is an API'.
tests.evidence: "Group, don't filter: product-attribute filters and `--dimension-key` are rejected." This is domain-specific knowledge, not generic explanation.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: While the body is detailed, the detail is procedural/rule-based rather than large reference tables; actual detailed lookup content (quota codes, API quirks, metric thresholds) is properly offloaded to references/ files, and the router table links out rather than embedding full detail.
tests.evidence: "How to read each API and metric: [collection-reference.md](references/collection-reference.md) (load it with any row)." shows detail is deferred to references.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file in references/ is linked via markdown link syntax somewhere in the body.
tests.evidence: "[cost-analysis.md](references/cost-analysis.md)", "[checks-model-invocation.md](references/checks-model-invocation.md)", "[cloudwatch-alarm-reference.md](references/cloudwatch-alarm-reference.md)", "[collection-reference.md](references/collection-reference.md)", "[api-quirks.md](references/api-quirks.md)", "[quota-codes.md](references/quota-codes.md)", "[metrics-and-logs.md](references/metrics-and-logs.md)" — all present. related-skills.md is also linked.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Reference links consistently specify when to load them, e.g. tied to specific steps or conditions.
tests.evidence: "Load when the step says so: [cost-analysis.md](references/cost-analysis.md) (Steps 3–5, before any LLM-COST or LLM-PT finding)"

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths of the form references/filename.md with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (read-only rules, cost labeling, quota lookup) are highly prescriptive with exact rules, while review judgment areas (e.g. deciding LLM-COST-003/004 applicability) are described with reasoning/criteria rather than rigid steps, matching prescriptiveness to fragility.
tests.evidence: "Never create, resize or delete Provisioned Throughput, never change a quota. Give the exact CLI or IaC and let the user run it." shows prescriptiveness calibrated to a fragile, risk-sensitive operation.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where multiple sources/approaches exist (e.g., pricing sources), a clear order of precedence/default is given rather than a flat list of equal options.
tests.evidence: "**Rates**, in order: the user (say so); `pricing:GetProducts` ... or the [pricing page] read with `verify_aws_claim`."

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable procedure (Steps 1-8) for reviewing any Bedrock cost/capacity scenario, with specific details (templates, check IDs) embedded within a reusable approach rather than being a one-off declaration.
tests.evidence: "Step 1: **Scope:** region(s), window, models and profiles; state the defaults chosen" generalizes across any review instance.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has an extensive 'Common wrong answers' section plus 'Error Handling' section documenting non-obvious pitfalls specific to this domain.
tests.evidence: "**"A `us.` profile bills as us-east-1."** It is a geographic routing scope; billing follows the source region (api-quirks §14, LLM-COST-005)."

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill provides a report template asset for its structured output deliverable.

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large inline output template exists in the body; the only mentioned template is the asset file referenced for full reports, and the quota table format shown inline is short.
tests.evidence: "**Report** the rows read as a table: | Quota name | Code | Applied value | Adjustable |, one row per quota" is a short inline format, well under 20 lines.

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: The single asset file is referenced in the body.

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: The asset reference specifies the condition for loading it (only for a full report), satisfying the when-to-load requirement.

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: The asset reference uses a relative path format from the skill root.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The procedural workflow is presented as a checkbox checklist with 'Step N:' labeling consistently, e.g. Step 1 through Step 8, matching the required format.
tests.evidence: "- [ ] Step 1: **Scope:** ..." through "- [ ] Step 8: Assemble the findings, then run \"Before You Present\"."

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an explicit self-validation section instructing the agent to check its own output before presenting it to the user.
tests.evidence: "## Before You Present — Validate Your Own Output\n\nA confidently wrong cost number is worse than a slow one. If an item can't be met, say so."
